p: Portsmouth's seaside side is Southsea, and it's well worth a trip once you've finished bouncing. The seafront has a long promenade, Clarence Pier with its family amusements and rides, and Southsea Castle, built by Henry VIII to defend the coast. Kids love exploring the castle walls and looking out over the Solent.
Nearby, the D-Day Story museum tells the story of the Normandy landings and the part Portsmouth played, and it's a moving and fascinating visit for older children and adults.
Fancy a quick island adventure? The hovercraft from Southsea to Ryde on the Isle of Wight is a fun and fast trip, and kids love the novelty of skimming across the water.
Literary fans might like to visit the Charles Dickens Birthplace Museum, where the famous author was born in 1812. It's a small museum that gives a glimpse into his early life.
Across the harbour in Gosport, the Royal Navy Submarine Museum lets you climb aboard a real submarine, and it's easy to reach on the Gosport Ferry from near Gunwharf Quays.
With so much to see, Portsmouth makes a cracking weekend destination, and the trampolines are a perfect way to start the day.

Flip Out's Harbour Gate spot is on the northern side of the city, so traffic heading down onto Portsea Island can be slow at peak times and on summer weekends. A good plan is to bounce first thing, then head south to Southsea for lunch by the sea, a walk along the front and an ice cream before the drive home. Gunwharf Quays also has plenty of family-friendly places to eat.
